text.p: These are the leading stories in the Albanian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOHA JONE

- Five people were killed and a dozen wounded when a drunken man carrying a grenade tripped as he got on to a bus in central Albania, causing an explosion. - Prime Minister Bashkim Fino failed to convince political parties to agree on a new electoral law, mostly due to the fact that President Sali Berisha's Democratic Party prefers a majority system to proportional representation.
- Five rightist parties threaten to boycott the elections if parliament, dominated by Berisha's Democrats, rejects a bill on a proportional electoral system.
- Socialist Party leader Fatos Nano launched his electoral campaign in Durres, where he accused Berisha of causing anarchy in the country.
GAZETA SHQIPTARE
- Unidentified people threw dynamite at a police station in the northern town of Shkoder.
- Masked gunmen set Gramshi town hall building ablaze for the third time since the beginning of the unrest.
- The Constitutional Court rejected a so-called anti-crime law passed by parliament, saying it ran counter to human rights.
- Would-be refugees who failed to reach Italy were given back the money they had paid to Albanian gangs controlling the trafficking.
ALBANIA
- Editorial attacks the Socialists and Prime Minister Fino, saying they allegedly pushed southern Albania into violence and anarchy by backing illegal local committees.
- The Socialist Party should observe a Council of Europe resolution to distance itself from rebel committees, Berisha told OSCE official Herbert Grubmayer.
- The health ministry announced a polio vaccination programme for children up to five years old started on May 5.
RILINDJA DEMOKRATIKE
- The OSCE's special envoy Franz Vranitzky arrives in Tirana on Wednesday to help political forces in preparing early elections due in June.
- The Democratic Party believes that the majority electoral system which is predominant in Europe is the best system for Albania, a Democrat leader, Ylli Vejsiu, said in an interview.

- The paper says Shkoder residents blame Prime Minister Fino for their repatriation as undesirables by Italy, saying Fino was taking revenge for not being allowed to enter the town by gunmen last month.
ZERI I POPULIT
- The Democratic Party is isolated and no other party wants to enter a coalition with it, paper says referring to rightest parties refusing to ally with the Democrats.
INDIPENDENT
- Democrat MPs are set to vote against a government draft law on elections, triggering a fall of the unity cabinet.
- During his visit to Washington next week, Fino will also meet International Monetary Fund officials.
